neet_che_u08_t09_1.working: In collision theory, a collision is effective only if the molecules have energy at or above the threshold energy and collide with proper orientation.

neet_che_u08_t09_3.working: The theory treats molecules as hard spheres and ignores their structure. This is corrected by introducing the steric (probability) factor P.

neet_che_u08_t09_4.working: Z_AB is the collision frequency (III). P is the orientation probability factor (II). e^(-Ea/RT) is the fraction of molecules with sufficient energy (I). P·Z_AB corresponds to the Arrhenius factor A (IV).

neet_che_u08_t09_5.working: A is true (hard spheres). B is false in the NCERT treatment, where P < 1 for complex molecules, although P > 1 is known in rare cases such as harpoon reactions. C is true. D is true (A ≈ P·Z_AB). E is false; the theory works better for simple species.
